Thought: I need to determine what gases are generated when thiocarbamates and dithiocarbamates decompose in aqueous solution. Let me think about the chemistry of these compounds.

Thiocarbamates have the general structure R-O-C(=S)-NR2, while dithiocarbamates have the structure R-S-C(=S)-NR2. When these compounds decompose in aqueous solution, they typically break down to release specific gases.

From my knowledge of organic chemistry, when thiocarbamates and dithiocarbamates decompose, they typically generate carbon disulfide (CS2) and amines (like methylamine). This is because the C=S bonds in these compounds can break down, releasing CS2, while the nitrogen-containing portion forms amines.

Looking at the options, option A (Carbon disulfide and methylamine) seems to be the most accurate description of the decomposition products.
Final Answer: The decomposition of thiocarbamates and dithiocarbamates in aqueous solution typically generates carbon disulfide (CS2) and amines such as methylamine. This occurs due to the breakdown of the C=S bonds in these compounds.
